title: Peak-flow disproportion provides no robust improvement in transported dry nocturnal cough prediction
abstract: The ratio FEV1/peak expiratory flow is an established upper-airway obstruction marker, but its usefulness for nonspecific nocturnal cough beyond conventional spirometry is uncertain. We tested log(FEV1/PEF) in separately recruited NHANES2007–2008 and2009–2010 adults. Weighted logistic models trained in3711 participants were frozen and evaluated in4158 participants. Beyond demographics, body size, smoking, FEV1, FVC and FEV1/FVC, target Brier changed from0.03993094 to0.03991870; delta-0.00001224, conditional target-PSU95% interval[-0.00001990,-0.00000381], joint-refit interval[-0.00005603,+0.00007148]. AUC changed by+0.000462. The tiny conditional gain was not robust to joint sampling uncertainty or strict volume-quality selection. This does not establish diagnostic usefulness, absence of airway physiology, or equivalence. Temporal survey transport is not independent clinical-cohort validation.
